posts.title: SEO vs AEO vs GEO: how to get found on Google and in AI answers
posts.excerpt: Search no longer ends on ten blue links. Here is what SEO, Answer Engine Optimization and Generative Engine Optimization each mean, and the checklist I use to cover all three.
body: People now get answers from Google's AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity and voice assistants, often without clicking a single result. Ranking still matters, but being the source those answers quote matters just as much. That is where AEO and GEO come in.

Search Engine Optimization makes your pages crawlable, fast, relevant and trusted so they rank in the normal results. Technical health, topical authority, internal links, backlinks and E-E-A-T are still the foundation. Without solid SEO, AEO and GEO have nothing to build on.
Answer Engine Optimization targets featured snippets, People Also Ask boxes and voice answers. The goal is a short, clear answer that a search engine can lift straight from your page.
Put the answer in the first 40 to 60 words under each question heading
Use question-style H2s and H3s that match how people search
Add FAQ, HowTo and Product schema where it fits
Keep one idea per paragraph so answers are easy to extract

Generative Engine Optimization is about being mentioned and cited when large language models build an answer. These systems favor content that is specific, well-structured and consistent across the web.
State facts with numbers, dates and sources that a model can quote
Make your brand an entity: consistent name, About page, Organization and Person schema, sameAs links
Earn mentions on trusted sites, directories and industry roundups
Publish original data, case studies and comparisons that others reference
Add an llms.txt file that points AI crawlers to your key pages
One plan that covers all three

In practice it is one workflow. Fix the technical base, build topic clusters around your money pages, write answer-first sections inside those pages, mark them up with schema, and keep your brand facts identical everywhere. Then track rankings in Search Console and test your key questions in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews every month to see where you are cited.
SEO gets you ranked, AEO gets you quoted, GEO gets you recommended. A modern search plan needs all three.

posts.title: Why your Shopify store is slow, and how to reach a 90+ PageSpeed score
posts.excerpt: Most slow Shopify stores have the same four problems: too many apps, oversized images, render-blocking scripts and a heavy theme. Here is the order I fix them in.
body: A slow store loses sales before the product page even finishes loading. On mobile, every extra second of load time lowers conversion, and Google uses Core Web Vitals as a ranking signal. The good news is that most Shopify speed problems come from the same few causes, and you can fix them without rebuilding the store.

Every app you install can add JavaScript and CSS to every page, even pages where the app does nothing. Open your theme code and search for scripts from apps you uninstalled months ago; they are often still there. Remove unused apps completely, then check that their snippets are gone from theme.liquid.
List every installed app and what it does for revenue
Uninstall anything that does not earn its place
Delete leftover snippets and script tags from the theme
Load chat widgets and review widgets only after user interaction
2. Serve images at the right size

A 3000px product photo shown in a 600px card is the most common waste I find. Use Shopify's image_url filter with a width, add srcset so phones get smaller files, and set width and height attributes so the layout does not jump while images load. Lazy-load everything below the first screen, but never the hero image.

Scripts in the head block the page from painting. Move non-critical scripts to the end of the body or add defer. Tracking pixels can usually load after the page is interactive without losing data, especially when you also send events server-side through the Conversions API.

Some themes ship sliders, animations and mega menus on every page. If your theme scores badly even with no apps installed, the theme itself is the bottleneck. Dawn-based themes are a strong starting point because they are built around native browser features instead of large libraries.

Test the home page, one collection page and one product page in PageSpeed Insights on mobile. Focus on Largest Contentful Paint (under 2.5s), Interaction to Next Paint (under 200ms) and Cumulative Layout Shift (under 0.1). Fix the worst page first, because that is usually where paid traffic lands.
Speed work is not a one-time job. Every new app or campaign script can undo it, so check your scores after every change.

posts.title: Topical mapping: how to plan SEO content that actually ranks
posts.excerpt: Writing random blog posts rarely builds rankings. A topical map groups every question your customers ask into clusters, so Google sees your site as the authority on the subject.
body: Google rewards sites that cover a subject completely. A single good article can rank for a while, but a connected set of pages that answer every related question builds rankings that last. That set of pages, planned in advance, is a topical map.

List the pages that make you money: service pages, category pages or product pages. Each one becomes the center of a cluster. Everything you write should support one of these pages and link back to it.

Pull questions from Google's People Also Ask boxes, Search Console queries, sales calls, support emails and competitor pages. Group them by the intent behind them, not by keyword. Questions that need the same answer belong on the same page.
Informational: what, why and how questions
Commercial: comparisons, best-of lists and costs
Transactional: service, product and location pages
Local: city and neighborhood variations, if you serve an area

Each cluster has one pillar page that covers the topic broadly and several supporting pages that go deep on one question each. Supporting pages link to the pillar, the pillar links to every supporting page, and the pillar links to the money page.

Publish the pillar and the supporting pages closest to buying intent first. Then fill in the informational pages. Publishing a full cluster within a few weeks sends a stronger signal than spreading one article a month across many topics.
Measure by cluster, not by post

In Search Console, filter pages by folder or keyword pattern and track total clicks for the whole cluster. A cluster that grows together is working. If one page gets impressions but no clicks, rewrite its title and meta description before writing anything new.
A topical map turns content from guesswork into a plan you can execute and measure.

posts.title: Google Ads for local service businesses: a call-first campaign setup
posts.excerpt: For plumbers, locksmiths, HVAC and movers, the phone call is the conversion. This is the campaign structure I use to lower cost per call without losing volume.
body: Local service customers rarely fill in forms. They search, see a number and call. A campaign built around calls, not clicks, usually produces cheaper leads and clearer reporting for these businesses.

Set up call conversions from ads, call conversions from the website using a Google forwarding number, and a minimum call length of 60 seconds so short wrong numbers do not count. Without this, Smart Bidding optimizes for the wrong thing.

Emergency searches such as "locksmith near me" or "burst pipe repair" behave differently from planned jobs like "AC installation quote". Put them in separate campaigns with separate budgets, schedules and ad copy. Emergency campaigns often deserve 24/7 scheduling and higher bids at night.
Emergency campaign: tight phrase and exact match, call assets, 24/7
Planned-work campaign: broader terms, landing page with quote form
Brand campaign: protects your name from competitors at low cost

Use "presence" location targeting, not "presence or interest", so you only pay for people who are actually in your service area. Add radius targeting around your base and exclude areas you do not serve.
Check the search terms report weekly at first. Add negatives for jobs, training, DIY, free and parts searches. In service accounts, this step alone often removes a large share of wasted spend.
Write ads that earn the call

Put the service, the area and the speed promise in the headline: "24/7 Locksmith in Brooklyn, 20-Min Arrival". Add call assets, location assets and a few sitelinks for the main services. Match the landing page headline to the ad so visitors know they are in the right place.
Measure cost per qualified call, not cost per click. That is the number the business owner cares about.
